Last July [Trudeau promised](http://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/justin-trudeau-vows-to-end-1st-past-the-post-voting-in-platform-speech-1.3114902) us that 2015 would be the last general election held under the first past the post system. It's a promise that (IMO) enticed a great many voters who had lost faith in the current system to cast a ballot in his favour (1).

We now find [Elections Canada saying](http://www.hilltimes.com/2016/03/08/elections-canada-concerned-about-holding-referendum-on-new-voting-system-implementing-changes-by-2019/53221) that it's passed time for Trudeau to get moving on this promise if they are expected to gear up for whatever it is we find on our next ballot.

>The Liberal government has promised to make changes to the way Canadians vote in general elections and that they would be in force by the next scheduled election in October 2019, but Elections Canada says it is concerned it won’t have enough time to implement electoral reform in time.

>According to the department’s 2016 Report on Plans and Priorities, tabled yesterday in the House of Commons, Elections Canada will begin to “establish the capacity it requires to support and implement electoral reform,” but makes it clear that in order to do so in time, the government needs to act quickly on implementing electoral changes.

>“Timely enactment and implementation of electoral reform are key to ensuring that changes are in place for the 2019 general election and that Canadians benefit from a high-quality electoral event that meets their expectations,” the report says.

Some possible outcomes if Elections Canada is to be believed, and I can see no reason why they should not be.

1. it is entirely possible that Trudeau has already made up his mind on which process we will use (I would say "propose" except that he holds a clear majority in The House and anything he *proposes* will pass) and the consultation process we were also promised will be more form and process than actual substance - *the electorate is unlikely to be happy.*

2. Trudeau's promised consultation process will be rushed, confusing, and disorganized and many who want to participate will not get a chance to do so as fully as they want - *the electorate is unlikely to be happy.*

3. a different system is instituted, there is either real or perceived confusion either at the ballot box or at Elections Canada and the results of the election are questioned - *the electorate is unlikely to be happy.*

4. the whole thing gets put off until a subsequent election - *the electorate is unlikely to be happy.*

5. Trudeau pulls a rabbit out of the hat - a reasonable majority of the electorate is happy

My look at the cards that Trudeau has dealt himself seems to indicate that he's either going to have to go all in on this -- and do so in a hurry -- or he's in trouble. _____

(1) *In the interests of full disclosure I wasn't one of them. On October 2015 I voted strategically by watching the polls and casting my ballot in favour of the non-CPC candidate most likely to either hold or win the riding I live in - yes, I was one of the "any party but a party lead by Stephen Harper" vote. That said, the party that did get my vote was also campaigning on electoral reform.*
The clock is ticking Mr. Trudeau, it's time to get cracking on that electoral reform promise
